messages:
maria: morning — noticed sustained queue growth on the us-west dedicated pool, hitting soft capacity around 60% and p99 tail spiking. thinking about switching from global FIFO to per-route queues or priority queues. thoughts? https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/fleet?panel=queued_requests

kai: saw it too. queued_requests jumped ~30 -> 120 in ~15m. p99 latency from ~250ms -> 1.8s. also some client retries piling up.

anna: per-route queues let us isolate embeddings-heavy traffic from chat and reranking. high-value routes can get reserved slots. tradeoff = more config + risk of uneven GPU utilization. :thinking:

miguel: agree with anna. alternative is priority queues with weights + admission control. sketch config below:
```
queues:
  - name: high-prio
    weight: 10
    soft_capacity: 50
  - name: default
    weight: 1
    soft_capacity: 200
admission:
  mode: reject_when_soft_full  # return 429 + Retry-After for best-effort routes
  retry_after_seconds: 3
```
This keeps FIFO semantics inside each queue but lets us shift dispatch ratios.

leah: for admission control, prefer 429 with Retry-After for external customers. for internal/enterprise we can expose longer queueing (and surface position). need to document how clients should backoff. also add a header `x-queued=true` when queued.

tariq: weighted fair queueing + aging is a good middle ground. aging prevents starvation of low-prio routes. pseudocode idea: on dequeue, if age(route) > threshold, temporarily boost effective weight. simple and easy to simulate.

ops-bot: [ALERT] us-west dedicated-pool saturation at 2023-10-14T09:15:02Z — capacity_util=0.78 queued=142

maria: proposal: implement per-route soft-limits + global backpressure policy. concrete rules:
- each route gets a soft queue limit (soft watermark). when exceeded, non-critical routes get 429s.
- a global hard cap protects GPU memory and KV cache pressure.
- use route weights to allocate burst tokens (e.g., weight ratio 10:1).
- add aging so long-waiting requests eventually get dispatched.
Metrics to implement: queued_requests_by_route, rejected_requests_by_route, avg_queue_wait_ms, head_of_line_delay_ms.

anna: SG. plan a canary in us-west-2 dedicated pool with 1% traffic under feature flag `queue_strategy=v1`. keep canary window 48h, rollback on >3% error uplift or p95 latency regression. add telemetry tag `queue_strategy=v1`.

kai: i'll add the feature flag + rollout playbook. also will run synthetic load tests for embeddings routes at 2x baseline to validate behavior.

miguel: i'll prototype a WFQ+aging simulation in the load harness and share results. will also try the admission mode `reject_when_soft_full` vs `queue_until_hard_full` to compare rejected vs queued tail costs.

maria: perfect. next steps: kai (rollout + playbook), miguel (sim + results), leah (retry semantics doc + headers), anna (canary ops). thanks all :thumbsup:
